problems.problem: Prose and content: the second half ends on “takes ‘this’ as what has been said above”, a pointer with no content, so the reading gives a reader nothing to hold beyond the reframing of the question. The plain sense also just echoes the key verse (“how it is known that it is so with all the beauties of existing things, and answers, by this”). Wang Bi’s own comment says what “above” refers to: 眾甫，物之始也。以無名說萬物始也 (the many beginnings are the beginnings of things, explained through the nameless), and then 言吾何以知萬物之始於無哉，以此知之也.
problems.fix: Keep the key and Wang Bi, but say what ‘this’ points back to, using his words on 以閱眾甫 and 以此. For example: “The chapter asks how the beauties of existing things are known to be so, and answers that it is by this; Wang Bi, on chapter 21, reads the question as how it is known that all things begin in non-being, and takes ‘this’ as the chapter’s preceding account of the nameless, by which all things begin.” Run entry-check again afterwards.
